Apart from the fact that this is quite healthy for a change of pace, I desperately need it, as all the driving has caused my tummy to develop into a bulge (it happens from driving so fast). results.translated_text: Prague, March 2nd, 1:36 AM. Babus, it was truly a great joy that you gave me with the photos. I had to look at them again and again because you received them. We really turned out funny, almost everyone. Unfortunately, it was an unforgivable mistake on my part with most of the pictures, despite using Pan film with a self-disc. As a result, many very nice little details have disappeared. Next time, something like that shouldn't happen again. Meanwhile, the films have also arrived, but there is still some excellent material available. You will get more. In any case, I would never have thought that Baba could be so pretty - of course, only in pictures. Is that due to the girl's photos or the photographer's skill? – Let's talk about the photos. Thank you very much, my dear. Once again, my birthday went very nicely and with gifts. There was a lot, including gramophone records, shirts, towel fabric, shawls, ties, perfume, etc., and from Ja Ellen a wonderful Montblanc fountain pen and lots of diligent writing, all in a case with a very nice letter. She only mentions my last letter very briefly, in which she considers part of it tasteless. But she didn't take it badly. She's going to Palestine this summer. Today I was at the Elekta Film Company, Prague 1, Narodny tr. 26 (Mr. Auerbach). He was very nice and will look through the book. He would have preferred it in German, but it will work this way too. If you have time off, send it to me or him. He also wants to send it to Berlin. He told me to contact various film producers. Well, we'll see. I have two more people here I'd like to show the book to. Of course, I'll leave all decisions regarding possible film rights up to them. I'm also sending the attached photos. Write to me soon and tell me how you're doing: how you're feeling and how it is. Lots of love, Bob. I'll send the film back in three weeks when I don't need it anymore. Elisabeth Aigner, Paris 15th arrondissement, 6.9 bis Rue Grancion, Prague 13th district, Ruska

results.translated_text: 8 days in Schönberg, September 30, 1935. I was at home this time, but only for 3 days involuntarily, as I had caught a bit of a cold. Now I feel better than before and am trying to work diligently. However, I will be staying longer on this trip, about 6 weeks. I am so far from Prague that it would be too tiring to drive back every Saturday. Your letter pleased me very much, especially your audacity, which you allowed yourself to do despite the censorship. Of course, I immediately went to the coffeehouse and admired your work; that is to say, I couldn't read it, but the photographs were pretty much the best that this paper had to offer. Very nice in the other newspaper. – I didn't find anything about E. You can imagine that I will always be happy when you are successful. But when it appears so clearly before you, it is something very special. Laci must have been very happy, very happy. I'll definitely keep my fingers crossed that your wish to earn at least 1000 francs a month comes true. But if it's not that much, don't be sad, darling. Rob will still love you. It's wonderful to have a lot of money, and it certainly contributes a great deal to complete happiness. Perhaps it's even necessary, but I'll never adjust to that. It makes one so easily spineless; I'd even go so far as to say that character suffers as one's ego grows. Not that I condemn it, quite the contrary. It's simply a sobering fact. But we've already discussed this at length. Right now, I'm sitting in a nice little restaurant, waiting for my train, which will take me even further. I'm traveling to Brno, Ostrava, and Bratislava in the next few days. But it's not just Bratislava that makes me happy on this journey, but that each day, each stop, brings me closer to the time when we can kiss each other tightly in our arms again. Yes, my love, you absolutely must make it possible for us to meet at Christmas. I don't know if I'll be able to find the time to travel later (from January 10th, 1936). That would be a real shame. And besides, with the time I have available, it's hardly possible to write (please excuse me, my train is coming soon). With love I therefore want to stop kissing. Please send any further mail by Saturday to the main post office in Moravská Ostrava, Czech Republic, for delivery to Prague.

results.translated_text: July 13, 1950 My dearest, you have no idea how I managed to get so far away from you. But sometimes I just get carried away. Fortunately, it's happening less and less often. I was so happy to talk to Feines on the phone. I hope you weren't too worried. I've been a little bit... Absolutely, it's always the same "nothing." Here's what happened at the doctor's. He was exceptionally kind. I tried to explain everything to him as objectively as possible. Apart from the fact that I already felt "completely normal" again, he naturally continued to reassure me and had the same effect on me, so that I felt like I did after the first visit with you. He only said that it's completely wrong to run away from these things; on the contrary, one should get used to them, because perhaps tomorrow someone else will tell me the same thing. It's much better to face them and deal with them on your own, even if it impresses you a lot at first. I think he's right. Anyway, that's the main thing, it's reassuring. I'll probably get your letter tomorrow. I don't need to tell you how much I'm looking forward to it. On Thursday, Ersi and I will be at the Randvers, which sends its warmest greetings to everyone. results.translated_text: My dearest, sweet Zabalein, I can't even tell you how happy your lovely gifts made me, and your letter. I was already over the miscarriage, just a little tired from the emotional strain. But after your letter, I think I've really changed. It was someone who shook me up and told me to pull myself together a little. Today I'm feeling very cheerful again (although actually, a 25th birthday shouldn't be a reason to be, it just reminds you how old you are and I've almost forgotten everything). But I think it's more a feeling of joy stemming from a certain excitement, having come away with relatively little damage. You resist thinking back on it with all your might because you really need that little bit of good cheer. Father is doing very, very well today; he's even allowed to go out a little tomorrow. It was particularly complicated for him because his appendix was fused to his main intestine. Mother had a bad cold and is almost completely recovered. But what proves I'm the old Rob again is that on Sunday I was driving around with some Chrysler obstacles. I just want to be with you, my dear, so you could see it for yourself. We were unfortunately in Freudenstadt and it was very nice. We've had a lot of snow for the last two days and I'll take advantage of the opportunity if possible. It won't be long now, because in 10 days I'll probably be... I have to travel again, which is awful. But this time I'm quite happy to go, although I don't know why, and a lot of work awaits me. In any case, I'm reacting with a certain optimism, the realization that there aren't only material things that could shake this foundation. At least for the moment. It's not always good to be like this. But I can't and won't change. When I'm sad, I'm really sad, and when I'm happy, it's usually exuberant and different; either I'm not working at all or I'm working hard. You don't have to notice this mood outwardly, it's still there. On my birthday, we were all alone at home and had a very nice chat. I was quite pleased that no one came, and so I went to bed early for the first time in a long time. I don't quite understand his fear of the Abitur (university entrance exam). You've worked quite well so far. A little bit of courage and a dash of cheekiness. Then you'll be fine. You're capable of both, so you'll manage. You mustn't let a certain amount of exam anxiety get the better of you. Let it be, it's usually much easier than you think. And if you're already working like this... Besides, I think it's important to be so consistent. In, failing. My dear, your high school diploma won't lift the bliss of a house. You can certainly help Laci just as much, if not more, without it, by being able to do it even earlier. Incidentally, it's at least as rare in England as it is at school in Paris. Or don't you think so? Zabalein, my dear, let me kiss you many times from your loving Rob.
